notable_absence.finding: howtos/n1ql-queries-with-sdk.md (this page) and howtos/sqlpp-queries-with-sdk.md (same directory, not in this batch) are near-duplicate pages of almost identical length (341 vs 336 lines) covering the same topic - running SQL++ queries via the SDK - with the same section structure verbatim (Getting Started, Queries & Placeholders, The Query Result, Query Options, Scan Consistency, Client Context ID, ReadOnly, Streaming Large Result Sets, Async APIs, Querying at Scope Level, Additional Resources). The only substantive differences: this page says 'Our query service uses SQL++ (formerly N1QL)' and tells the reader to use the cbq shell tool to create a primary index; sqlpp-queries-with-sdk.md drops the N1QL parenthetical entirely and tells the reader to use the Admin UI's Query tab instead, and adds a 'SQL++ Compared to Key-Value' tip box this page lacks. Critically, NEITHER page links to, mentions, or otherwise acknowledges the other's existence anywhere in its body - there is no supersedes, renamedFrom, or retainedForLegacyCompatibility statement on either page, and this page does not tell the reader to use sqlpp-queries-with-sdk.md instead (so mustUseInsteadWhen is explicitly NOT warranted here, contrary to what a page-level rename convention might lead one to expect). This reads as an un-pruned legacy duplicate left behind after a page-level rename-and-partial-rewrite (N1QL -> SQL++ terminology, cbq -> Admin UI instructions), not a deliberate redirect/alias stub (which would be short and point at the other page) and not genuinely different content (the two are near word-for-word twins).
